terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Approximate three-quarter camera from the single reference; the production portfolio camera remains authoritative for framing.

objectClass.notes: Stylized real-time browser reconstruction. The visible shell, front glazing, frame, seats, and control details are authoritative; hidden rear/service geometry is inferred.

reasoning: The reference shows a continuous rounded outer shell containing an inset front-frame and glazing assembly.
Two multi-part seats, three pane divisions, repeated frame members, and several small controls require a three-level hierarchy.
Glass, painted shell, graphite frame, upholstery, brushed metal, rubber seals, and emissive status elements require distinct material responses.
The requested runtime needs semantic parts, animation anchors, click targets, and an explodable hierarchy without exceeding the existing browser budget.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

details.description: Broad-radius upper-left shell return rounds into the front opening instead of ending in a square corner.
A shallow horizontal top-crown seam separates the outer cap from the front shell return.
The visible lateral shell extends almost the full front width in depth and keeps the same softened rear corner language.
A continuous graphite reveal sits inside the white shell and behind its front lip around the entire glazed opening.
Two narrow vertical graphite mullions divide the front into three glazing sections and contact both header and sill.
A slim vertical handle and small hinge blocks stand off from the right-hand door frame.
A dark continuous plinth sits inside the lower white shell return and grounds the glazed front.
Two high-back seats include separate headrests, backrests, cushions, armrests, central pedestals, and radial feet.
A thin dark door seal traces the lower glazing edge above the base plinth.
The front glazing has a neutral smoked tint that preserves interior-seat contrast without becoming opaque.
Seat upholstery is darker and rougher than the graphite frame and has softer highlight falloff.
The white shell uses a satin painted finish whose grazing highlights reveal the rounded corners without mirror reflections.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The chamber reads as one softened rectangular enclosure with visible side depth, not a stack of square slabs.
The front opening is recessed behind a dark reveal and split into three glazed sections by attached mullions.
Two high-back seats with headrests, cushions, armrests, and pedestal feet remain recognizable through the glazing at the authored Oxygen camera.
Door handle, lower sill, base plinth, screen recess, hinge blocks, and cyan status line survive the portfolio camera distance.
Painted shell, graphite frame, glass, upholstery, and brushed metal have visibly distinct roughness and value response under neutral laboratory lighting.
The hierarchy remains clickable and explodable, all target viewports remain framed, and every detail tier stays within its existing triangle/drawable/material/texture budget.

featureGroups.name: Continuous rounded enclosure silhouette
qualityCriteria: The outer shell forms a single softened rectangular mass with broad corner radii and visible lateral depth.
The inset dark opening preserves a consistent shell border on the top, sides, and lower sill.
failureModes: outer shell reads as five disconnected wall slabs
front opening is flush with the facade or loses the broad corner returns

featureGroups.name: Front glazing and interior hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Outer shell, front reveal, three panes, mullions, door hardware, base, and two seats remain separately named parts.
The seats sit behind the glazing and attach to the chamber floor rather than floating in front of it.
failureModes: glazing renders as one opaque gray wall
seats or mullions disappear at the authored Oxygen camera

featureGroups.name: Door, handle, seat, and frame attachments
qualityCriteria: Door handle, hinge blocks, mullions, headrests, armrests, and seat pedestals overlap or socket into their parent parts with no visible gaps.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Shell, glass, upholstery, and metal separation
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Neutral laboratory look development
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Inset frame, three glazing sections, and attached hardware
Paired high-back seat readability through glass
Shell, frame, glass, upholstery, and metal separation

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

runtimeEvidence.rotationRegression: tests/scene-detail.test.mjs#oxygen door group rotates its real panel about the right hinge axis
runtimeEvidence.parityRegression: tests/scene-detail.test.mjs#sculpt spec interaction hierarchy and proxies match production metadata

assumptions: Rear service panels continue the plain satin-white shell because no rear reference is available.
The right front section is treated as the semantic door; exact hinge mechanics remain approximate.
Glass uses a real-time smoked-transparent approximation with no caustic or exact thickness claim.
Seat backs and pedestal feet continue symmetrically where occluded.

proceduralStrategy: Build one shared rounded hard-surface geometry for enclosure and device chassis masses.

Keep material channels independent and constrain glass opacity so the seat hierarchy remains visible.
Expose nodes, sockets, colliders, and part metadata through root.userData.sculptRuntime.
Trim only micro detail by performance tier; never replace identity-defining rounded silhouettes with boxes.
